pages.text: Crunch-crunch echoes in a misty forest. Ping the panda sits like a cozy pillow, ready for bamboo breakfast.
Ping is a mammal, so she has fur and drinks milk when she is a baby panda.
Bamboo stalks are her favorite. Bamboo is a grass, and pandas eat lots of it every day.
Chewing bamboo takes work. Ping’s strong jaws and big teeth help crush the tough, crunchy stems.
She lives in mountain forests where bamboo grows well. Cool air and tall trees make good panda homes.
Ping’s black-and-white fur helps her blend with shadows and bright patches of light in the woods.
After eating, Ping climbs a low tree branch carefully. Pandas can climb, especially when they are young.
Ping rests often to save energy. Bamboo has low energy, so pandas eat and rest a lot.
A small stream gurgles nearby. Ping drinks and then returns to her bamboo patch like it is her pantry.
Bedtime thought: pandas are gentle bamboo eaters, living in mountain forests with special fur patterns.
